title_en: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after the GOP's midterm wipeout
title_zh: 尽管特朗普在共和党中期惨败后心存疑虑，但移民逮捕行动有增无减
summary: In the wake of midterm elections, President Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the Democrats
summary_zh: 中期选举结束后，唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他的移民镇压可能“过于严厉”，并表示是时候坐下来了
body_en: In the wake of midterm elections, President Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the Democrats
By VALERIE GONZALEZ Associated Press and TIM SULLIVAN Associated Press
It’s business as usual for President Donald Trump's deportation offensive despite the Republican wipeout in the midterm elections.

In Los Angeles, masked immigration officers in body armor blocked a hospital emergency room driveway in a heavily Latino neighborhood early Saturday. In central Alabama, twin 19-year-old brothers from Venezuela were arrested while driving back to college a day after the election.
Advocates reported arrests from California to Michigan to Massachusetts.
After Democrats trounced the GOP and won control of the next Congress, Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party.
“I’d love to do something on immigration,” he said in an interview with CBS “60 Minutes” recorded Friday.

Hours later, he named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration agenda, as his new chief of staff. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said his orders had not changed.

“Deportations will continue,” Mullin wrote in an online post the day after the election, warning that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement takes no days off and that “this includes on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and Election Day.”
María Bilbao, a campaign coordinator for the American Friends Service Committee in Miami, said she has received at least one call a day from someone detained in South Florida since the election.
“Everything remains exactly the same. The arrests have not ceased at all,” Bilbao said.

Florida Highway Patrol officers and ICE agents have detained people in their cars, as well as places including supermarkets, pharmacies and gas stations. Immigrants under supervision have also been arrested when they showed up at ICE's Miami office for their appointments.
Erick Gasca, 31, got home Friday night after an evening playing board games with friends. He lives near Adventist Health White Memorial Medical Center in Los Angeles.
An “unprecedented” number of vehicles with tinted windows and no license plates were parked near the hospital's emergency room entrance, he said.
“I thought they were going to raid the hospital or something,” he recalled.

The Department of Homeland Security declined to explain the officers’ presence there, though Bill Essayli, the top Justice Department prosecutor in Los Angeles, said they were bringing a detainee for medical treatment. Essayli said two people were arrested for assaulting federal agents.
“ICE does not target hospitals, schools, or churches,” DHS said in a statement.
The agents' presence attracted some 30 residents and passersby. Footage shot by Gasca’s cousin, Michelle Rivera, shows protesters shouting and officers pinning someone down.

“White Memorial does not participate in immigration enforcement,” hospital president Daniel Fontoura said in a statement, adding it would not let such activities "compromise our commitment to patient care and safety.”
body_zh: 中期选举结束后，唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，他的移民镇压可能“过于严厉”，并建议是时候与民主党坐下来了
瓦莱丽·冈萨雷斯 (VALERIE GONZALEZ) 美联社和蒂姆·苏利文 (TIM SULLIVAN) 美联社报道
尽管共和党在中期选举中惨败，但唐纳德·特朗普总统的驱逐攻势照常进行。
在洛杉矶，周六早些时候，身着防弹衣的蒙面移民官员封锁了拉丁裔人口密集的社区的一家医院急诊室车道。在阿拉巴马州中部，选举后一天，一对来自委内瑞拉的 19 岁双胞胎兄弟在开车返回大学时被捕。
倡导者报告称，从加利福尼亚州到密歇根州再到马萨诸塞州都有逮捕事件。
在民主党击败共和党并赢得下一届国会的控制权后，特朗普表示他的移民镇压可能“过于严厉”，并建议是时候与对手坐下来了。
“我很乐意在移民问题上做点什么，”他在周五录制的哥伦比亚广播公司“60 分钟”节目中说道。
几个小时后，他任命其强硬移民议程的设计师斯蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)为他的新任幕僚长。与此同时，国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林表示，他的命令没有改变。
“驱逐出境将继续，”穆林在选举后第二天在网上发帖写道，警告美国移民和海关执法局没有休息日，“这包括感恩节、圣诞节和选举日。”
迈阿密美国公谊服务委员会的竞选协调员玛丽亚·毕尔巴鄂表示，自大选以来，她每天至少接到一个来自南佛罗里达州被拘留者的电话。
“一切都保持原样。逮捕行动根本没有停止，”毕尔巴鄂说。
佛罗里达州高速公路巡逻人员和 ICE 特工在车内以及超市、药店和加油站等地方拘留了人们。受到监管的移民在前往 ICE 迈阿密办事处赴约时也遭到逮捕。
31 岁的埃里克·加斯卡 (Erick Gasca) 周五晚上与朋友玩了一晚棋盘游戏后回到家。他住在洛杉矶基督复临安息日会怀特纪念医疗中心附近。
他说，医院急诊室入口附近停着数量“史无前例”的有色车窗且没有牌照的车辆。
“我以为他们会突击搜查医院什么的，”他回忆道。
尽管洛杉矶司法部最高检察官比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 表示，他们正在带一名被拘留者接受治疗，但国土安全部拒绝解释这些警官的存在。埃萨利说，有两人因袭击联邦特工而被捕。
国土安全部在一份声明中表示：“ICE 不针对医院、学校或教堂。”
特工的出现吸引了大约30名居民和路人。加斯卡的表弟米歇尔·里维拉拍摄的视频显示，抗议者大喊大叫，警察将某人按倒。
医院院长丹尼尔·丰图拉（Daniel Fontoura）在一份声明中表示，“怀特纪念医院不参与移民执法”，并补充说，医院不会让此类活动“损害我们对患者护理和安全的承诺”。

summary: Driver, 61, faces DUI and murder charges after Tuesday crash critically injuring two others in North Hollywood A driver who reportedly crashed into pedestrians on a Los Angeles corner during Tuesday rush hour, killing three people and critically injuring two m

body_en: Driver faces DUI and murder charges after three killed in LA crash, officials say | Los Angeles
Driver, 61, faces DUI and murder charges after Tuesday crash critically injuring two others in North Hollywood

A driver who reportedly crashed into pedestrians on a Los Angeles corner during Tuesday rush hour, killing three people and critically injuring two more, was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence and three counts of murder, police said on Wednesday.
The fatal crash took place near a North Hollywood metro station.

The driver, identified as Ihor Demianenko, 61, was treated for minor injuries at a hospital, according to police. He was booked early on Wednesday, with bail set at $6m. Authorities said the driver was able to talk but appeared to be in shock after Tuesday’s crash.

A local CBS News affiliate station reported that the ‌car crashed into a food stand near a bus stop along a major ​thoroughfare, Lankershim Boulevard, that runs through the busy NoHo commercial and arts district in the city’s San Fernando valley.
The three women who died were between the ages of 40 and 60, according to the police news release. Authorities haven’t released their names. The two injured women are in their 50s.
The LA mayor, Karen Bass, said the victims included street vendors and pedestrians.
“I’m heartbroken for the families of everyone impacted,” she said in a post on X.
Authorities will be checking the video in the area in what will be a “prolonged but very deliberate investigation”, said LA police chief Jim McDonnell.
Aerial news video footage of ⁠the scene showed a white, partially crumpled, ​small ​SUV that appeared ​to have run up on to the sidewalk and ​into the side of a mass-transit shelter structure.
Reuters and Associated Press contributed reporting

周二北好莱坞发生车祸，造成另外两人重伤，61 岁司机面临酒后驾车和谋杀指控

这起致命车祸发生在北好莱坞地铁站附近。
据警方称，这名司机名叫伊霍尔·德米亚年科 (Ihor Demianenko)，61 岁，受轻伤，正在医院接受治疗。他于周三早些时候被登记，保释金为 600 万美元。当局表示，周二的事故发生后，司机能够说话，但看上去很震惊。
当地哥伦比亚广播公司新闻附属电台报道称，这辆汽车撞上了兰克希姆大道主干道上公交车站附近的一个食品摊，该大道穿过该市圣费尔南多山谷繁忙的 NoHo 商业和艺术区。
据警方新闻稿称，三名死亡女性年龄在 40 岁至 60 岁之间。当局尚未公布他们的名字。两名受伤妇女均为50多岁。
洛杉矶市长凯伦·巴斯表示，受害者包括街头小贩和行人。
“我为每个受到影响的人的家人感到心碎，”她在 X 上的一篇帖子中说道。
洛杉矶警察局长吉姆·麦克唐纳表示，当局将在该地区检查视频，这将是一次“长期但非常审慎的调查”。
现场的航拍新闻视频显示，一辆白色的、部分皱巴巴的小型SUV似乎跑到了人行道上，并撞上了公共交通候车亭的一侧。

body_en: Death of Javits Frimpong, who moved to the US from Ghana a year ago, has affected close-knit Ghanaian community
A 17-year-old boy has been arrested and charged with murder in connection with the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong in the Bronx.

The teenager was taken from his Bronx home for questioning Wednesday morning and brought to the New York City police department (NYPD)’s 42nd precinct. The suspect, whose identity has not been released, faces several charges, including murder, manslaughter, criminal possession of a weapon and other firearm-related offenses.

Investigators had previously been searching for three teenage boys believed to be connected to the shooting. Authorities have not ruled out the possibility of additional arrests. It remains unclear whether the suspect and the victim knew one another.
The arrest took place just hours before attorneys representing Frimpong’s family held a news conference in Harlem.

The deadly incident occurred on 29 October near Crotona Park in the Bronx. Officers responded to a shooting report at approximately 9.24am and discovered Frimpong suffering from a gunshot wound to his abdomen, according to the NYPD.
The 15-year-old was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he was pronounced dead. Police initially reported that no arrests had been made as investigators searched for three teenage suspects.

Surveillance video reportedly showed Frimpong running while someone dressed entirely in black followed him. Footage from another camera angle appeared to capture masked individuals wearing dark clothing running away from the scene.
Frimpong’s death has deeply affected members of the Bronx’s close-knit Ghanaian community, as well as students at DreamYard Preparatory School, where he was in his sophomore year.

The teenager had moved to the US from Ghana a year earlier to reunite with his father, who works as a taxi driver. His killing occurred around the time he was marking his first anniversary of living in New York.
Frimpong’s father remembered his son as “clever” and “quiet”. He also said the teenager had been experiencing bullying at DreamYard Preparatory School.
As the investigation continues, the family has hired civil rights attorney Ben Crump to represent them.

“A juvenile suspect has reportedly been charged in connection with Javits’ killing,” Crump said in a statement . “While these charges mark an important step toward accountability, the questions remain: Why did this happen, and could it have been prevented? His family deserves answers and justice.”
body_zh: 一年前从加纳移居美国的贾维茨·弗林蓬 (Javits Frimpong) 的去世影响了紧密的加纳社区
一名 17 岁男孩因涉嫌在布朗克斯区枪杀 15 岁贾维茨·福林蓬 (Javits Frimpong) 事件而被捕，并被指控犯有谋杀罪。
周三早上，这名少年被从布朗克斯的家中带走接受讯问，并被带到纽约市警察局 (NYPD) 第 42 分局。嫌疑人的身份尚未公布，他面临多项指控，包括谋杀、过失杀人、非法持有武器和其他与枪支有关的罪行。
调查人员此前一直在寻找三名据信与枪击事件有关的男孩。当局并未排除进一步逮捕的可能性。目前尚不清楚嫌疑人和受害人是否认识。
逮捕发生前几个小时，代表弗林蓬家人的律师在哈莱姆区召开新闻发布会。
这起致命事件于 10 月 29 日发生在布朗克斯克罗托纳公园附近。据纽约警察局称，警方于上午 9 点 24 分左右接到枪击报告，发现弗林蓬腹部受枪伤。
这名 15 岁的男子被送往附近的一家医院，但在那里被宣布死亡。警方最初报告称，调查人员在搜寻三名青少年嫌疑人时并未逮捕任何人。
据报道，监控视频显示，Frimpong 奔跑着，身后跟着一个全黑衣服的人。从另一个摄像机角度拍摄的视频似乎捕捉到穿着深色衣服的蒙面人逃离现场。
弗林蓬的去世深深影响了布朗克斯关系密切的加纳社区的成员，以及他就读二年级的 DreamYard 预科学校的学生。
这名少年一年前从加纳移居美国，与担任出租车司机的父亲团聚。他的被杀发生在他庆祝在纽约生活一周年之际。
弗林蓬的父亲记得他的儿子“聪明”且“安静”。他还表示，这名少年在 DreamYard 预科学校遭受了欺凌。
随着调查的继续，这家人聘请了民权律师本·克伦普（Ben Crump）代表他们。
克伦普在一份声明中说：“据报道，一名少年嫌疑人因涉嫌杀害贾维茨而受到指控。” “虽然这些指控标志着追究责任的重要一步，但问题仍然存在：为什么会发生这种情况，是否可以避免？他的家人应该得到答案和正义。”

body_en: Voters in Providence, Rhode Island, chose to pull foreign investments from countries that profit from genocide
The tectonic blue wave that washed over the country in last week’s midterms also brought about a historic night for the pro-Palestine movement.

Up and down the ballot, candidates who demanded an end to Israel’s war in Gaza resoundingly defeated opponents funded by the pro-Israel lobbying group American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac).

Providence, meanwhile, became the second US city to vote to divest from Israel. Voters in the Rhode Island capital approved a ballot measure last Tuesday requiring the city to refrain from investing in foreign countries that profit from “genocide, apartheid, ethnic cleansing and prolonged military occupation”.

Passing with 75% of the vote, the victory aligns with public opinion’s souring on the Israeli government. One-third of Americans – including a similar share of Jews – say Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians , and more than half say they want the government to stop sending weapons to Israel, according to recent polls. Organizers say the success of Providence’s ballot strategy is built on both the broad public support for divestment and a canvassing operation that can be replicated by pro-Palestinian groups in other cities.

“When we were out on the streets, we were overwhelmed by the positive results, by people who were so thankful to have a meaningful opportunity to do something about Palestine,” said Adit Sabnis, a graduate student at Brown University and local union organizer with the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) Local 6516, one of the groups that led the Providence ballot push. “This is an overwhelmingly pro-Palestine and anti-genocide city.”

The Providence for Palestine campaign launched a little less than a year ago with just 40 volunteers, said Zack Kligler, an organizer with Jewish Voice for Peace – Rhode Island. Led by the local chapters of Jewish Voice for Peace, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), AFT and American Muslims for Palestine, as well as the local housing justice organization Reclaim RI, the group decided to pursue a ballot strategy after traditional legislative efforts failed.

In 2024, then-mayor Brett Smiley and other city councilors blocked an ordinance to divest from Israel , and officials at Brown University, an Ivy League school in the city, rejected a similar student-led proposal. At least $2.5m in city funds were invested in companies directly profiting from what organizers call a genocide in Gaza and Israeli apartheid. The city also held more than $2m in Israeli bonds as recently as 2022.

Over the spring and summer, the coalition collected more than 10,000 signatures – twice the required threshold to qualify the measure. Organizers then built out an enormous canvassing operation, with nearly 300 volunteers stationed at street corners, businesses and community events across the city. Leading up to the midterms, they knocked on 17,000 doors, made 18,000 phone calls and talked to 30,000 neighbors about what’s happening in Gaza and what divestment entails.

Jackie Goldman, an incoming Providence city councilor and key organizer for the divestment measure, said few voters at the start of the campaign season knew of the city’s investments in companies with Israeli ties. But upon learning about the ballot initiative, Goldman said, most people were eager to support and saw divestment as “an empowering action”.
Though a broad coalition of Providence residents came together in support of divestment, the campaign was powered by many Jewish organizers and voters.

“It’s a demonstration that the idea that US Jews are in line behind Israel is just absolutely false,” said Kligler. “We ended up mobilizing Jews across the city, and we won every ward, including the most heavily Jewish ones.”

Organizers say the overwhelming success of the measure was bolstered by the electoral victories of a slate of progressive, pro-Palestinian candidates in the city’s September primary, including Goldman and mayor-elect David Morales, a DSA member who defeated Smiley. Both candidates gathered signatures for the measure while canvassing for their own campaigns.

But rather than pro-Palestinian groups endorsing specific candidates, Kligler said, Providence has shown that advocates themselves can take a more proactive role in shaping legislation: “This is a case of not just the movement getting behind candidates – it’s the movement forwarding its own policy priorities and pulling candidates behind it.”

Kligler said one of the top priorities for Providence organizers was creating a replicable blueprint for other cities. The Providence for Palestine coalition posted a call on Instagram encouraging organizers across the country to reach out and discuss the lessons and tactics from the city’s win. Kligler said the coalition was not actively working on another ballot effort yet, but organizers in different cities had reached out.

Providence organizers themselves studied ballot efforts in Somerville, Massachusetts – the first US city last year to vote to divest from Israel – and Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, where a divestment referendum was blocked by a legal challenge. Kligler said Pittsburgh organizers were especially helpful in providing guidance on how to check that addresses were correctly written and petitions were signed in acceptable colors so that they couldn’t be disqualified based on a technicality.
A handful of other cities, most recently Cambridge, Massachusetts, have also divested from companies with Israeli ties through city council resolutions, not by popular vote.

On election night, officials in Palm Beach county, Florida – the world’s largest local government investor in Israeli bonds – also voted not to reinvest $67.5m in bonds that had matured on 1 November. The decision followed months of sustained organizing from local activists with the “Our Taxes, Our Needs” campaign, who sued the county and showed up in droves to board meetings, putting pressure on officials.

Advocates are looking to block three more investments in Palm Beach that are set to expire over the next couple of years, said Lydia Ghuman, executive director of the Internationalist Law Center, which has been leading the county’s effort to divest from Israel. The next step is to pass policies redirecting these bond investments into housing, education, healthcare and other local needs – a more appropriate use of taxpayer funds than enabling violence, Ghuman said.
body_zh: 罗德岛州普罗维登斯的选民选择撤回从种族灭绝中获利的国家的外国投资
上周中期选举席卷全国的构造性蓝色浪潮也为亲巴勒斯坦运动带来了历史性的夜晚。
在选票上下，要求以色列结束加沙战争的候选人彻底击败了由亲以色列游说团体美国以色列公共事务委员会（Aipac）资助的反对者。
与此同时，普罗维登斯成为第二个投票从以色列撤军的美国城市。罗德岛州首府的选民上周二批准了一项投票措施，要求该市避免投资于从“种族灭绝、种族隔离、种族清洗和长期军事占领”中获利的外国。
这次胜利以 75% 的选票获得通过，这与公众舆论对以色列政府的不满一致。根据最近的民意调查，三分之一的美国人——包括类似比例的犹太人——表示以色列对巴勒斯坦人实施了种族灭绝，超过一半的人表示他们希望政府停止向以色列运送武器。组织者表示，普罗维登斯投票策略的成功建立在公众对撤资的广泛支持和拉票行动的基础上，其他城市的亲巴勒斯坦团体可以效仿。
布朗大学研究生、美国教师联合会 (AFT) Local 6516 的当地工会组织者阿迪特·萨布尼斯 (Adit Sabnis) 说：“当我们走上街头时，我们对积极的结果感到不知所措，人们非常感激有一个有意义的机会为巴勒斯坦做点什么。”该组织是普罗维登斯投票推动的领导团体之一。 “这是一座绝大多数支持巴勒斯坦和反种族灭绝的城市。”
犹太和平之声罗德岛组织的组织者扎克·克利格勒 (Zack Kligler) 表示，“为巴勒斯坦普罗维登斯”运动是在不到一年前发起的，当时只有 40 名志愿者。在犹太和平之声、美国民主社会主义者 (DSA)、AFT 和美国穆斯林支持巴勒斯坦分会以及当地住房正义组织 Reclaim RI 当地分会的领导下，该组织在传统立法努力失败后决定采取投票策略。
2024年，时任市长布雷特·斯迈利和其他市议员阻止了一项从以色列撤资的法令，该市常春藤盟校布朗大学的官员也拒绝了一项由学生主导的类似提案。至少有 250 万美元的城市资金投资于直接从组织者所说的加沙种族灭绝和以色列种族隔离中获利的公司。截至 2022 年，该市还持有超过 200 万美元的以色列债券。
在春季和夏季，该联盟收集了超过 10,000 个签名——是该措施资格要求门槛的两倍。随后，组织者开展了大规模的拉票活动，近 300 名志愿者驻扎在全市的街角、企业和社区活动中。在中期选举之前，他们敲开了 17,000 个门，拨打了 18,000 个电话，并与 30,000 名邻居谈论了加沙正在发生的事情以及撤资意味着什么。
即将上任的普罗维登斯市议员和撤资措施的主要组织者杰基·戈德曼表示，在竞选季节开始时，很少有选民知道该市对与以色列有联系的公司的投资。但高盛表示，在了解投票倡议后，大多数人都渴望支持，并将撤资视为“一种赋权行动”。
尽管普罗维登斯居民组成了广泛的联盟，支持撤资，但这场运动是由许多犹太组织者和选民推动的。
克利格勒说：“这表明美国犹太人站在以色列一边的想法是绝对错误的。” “我们最终动员了全城的犹太人，我们赢得了每个选区，包括犹太人最多的选区。”
组织者表示，该措施取得压倒性成功的原因是一系列进步的、亲巴勒斯坦的候选人在该市 9 月份的初选中取得了选举胜利，其中包括高盛和当选市长大卫·莫拉莱斯 (David Morales)，后者是一位击败了史迈利的 DSA 成员。两位候选人在为自己的竞选活动拉票时都收集了该措施的签名。
但克利格勒表示，普罗维登斯并不是亲巴勒斯坦团体支持特定候选人，而是表明倡导者本身可以在制定立法方面发挥更积极的作用：“这不仅仅是运动支持候选人的情况，也是运动推进自己的政策优先事项并将候选人拉到背后的情况。”
克利格勒表示，普罗维登斯组织者的首要任务之一是为其他城市制定可复制的蓝图。巴勒斯坦普罗维登斯联盟在 Instagram 上发出呼吁，鼓励全国各地的组织者伸出援手，讨论该市获胜的教训和策略。克利格勒表示，该联盟尚未积极开展另一次投票工作，但不同城市的组织者已经伸出援手。
普罗维登斯组织者自己研究了马萨诸塞州萨默维尔（去年美国第一个投票从以色列撤资的城市）和宾夕法尼亚州匹兹堡的投票情况，那里的撤资公投因法律挑战而受阻。克利格勒表示，匹兹堡的组织者在如何检查地址是否正确书写以及请愿书是否以可接受的颜色签署方面提供了特别有用的指导，这样他们就不会因为技术问题而被取消资格。
其他一些城市，最近是马萨诸塞州的剑桥，也通过市议会决议，而不是通过民众投票，从与以色列有联系的公司中撤资。
在选举之夜，佛罗里达州棕榈滩县（全球最大的以色列债券地方政府投资者）的官员也投票决定不对 11 月 1 日到期的 6750 万美元债券进行再投资。这一决定是在当地活动人士持续组织“我们的税收，我们的需求”运动数月之后做出的，他们起诉了该县，并成群结队地出席董事会会议，给官员们带来了压力。
国际主义法律中心执行董事莉迪亚·古曼表示，支持者正在寻求阻止棕榈滩另外三项投资，这些投资将在未来几年内到期。国际主义法律中心一直在领导棕榈滩从以色列撤资的努力。古曼说，下一步是通过政策，将这些债券投资转向住房、教育、医疗保健和其他当地需求——这是对纳税人资金的更适当的使用，而不是助长暴力。

body_en: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/read-the-letter-the-white-houses-top-lawyer-sent-rep-garcia-over-threats-to-investigate-trump

The White House's top lawyer sent a letter of warning to incoming House Oversight Committee chair Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., on Wednesday, claiming that the Democrats' promise to investigate the Trump administration "may cross the line into blatant criminality."

White House counsel William Scharf wrote Garcia a three-page letter to "remind" him of the constitutional limits of congressional investigations, "which you and members of the new Congress have evinced a clear intent to transgress."
The letter, obtained by PBS News, accuses Democrats of "abusive and capricious threats" against President Donald Trump and members of his administration.
Read the full letter by clicking the image below.

On election night, after projections showed Democrats would control the House of Representatives in the incoming Congress, Garcia addressed the Trump administration with a two-word statement : "Lawyer up."
WATCH: Rep. Garcia says voters gave Democrats a mandate to pursue accountability
On the PBS News Hour last week, White House correspondent Liz Landers asked Garcia whether he felt voters gave Democrats a mandate to investigate the Trump administration.

"The American public are looking at their own bills and seeing costs go up when they go to the supermarket, yet they're seeing the Trumps get richer. And so that's a real contrast, and that's a real issue for us to take on," he added later in the interview.
WATCH: Trump's $2B income in 2025 raises fresh questions about profiting off presidency
Garcia hasn't dropped that sentiment after Scharf's letter.

"It appears Donald Trump has something to hide," Garcia said in a statement on Wednesday. "We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President's lawyers."

title_en: Judge allows Trump defamation case against BBC to proceed but tosses 1 claim
title_zh: 法官允许特朗普针对 BBC 的诽谤案继续审理，但驳回 1 项索赔
summary: President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation case against the BBC remains on track for now
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统针对 BBC 提起的价值 100 亿美元的诽谤案目前仍在进行中
body_en: President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation case against the BBC remains on track for now
President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation case against the BBC remains on track, for the moment.

A federal judge in Florida ruled on Tuesday that Trump’s defamation claim could go forward, though he did not rule on the merits. The publicly funded British broadcaster had sought to dismiss the case.
Judge Jeffrey Kuntz did dismiss part of the case, tossing out a Trump claim that the BBC’s actions violated a Florida law concerning unfair business practices.

Trump filed his lawsuit against the BBC in December . The Republican president accused the BBC of defamation as well as deceptive and unfair trade practices related to a documentary, “Trump: A Second Chance?”

The BBC acknowledged that filmmakers spliced together quotes from different sections of the speech Trump delivered to his supporters on Jan. 6, 2021 , before the storming of the U.S. Capitol, to make it seem that Trump was directly urging violence.

The broadcaster apologized over the editing , and that was something the judge made note of in his ruling Wednesday. The head of the BBC and its top news executive both resigned. The BBC has denied Trump’s claims that it defamed him.

In October, a different judge in Florida ordered Trump to sit for a deposition in the case by Dec. 11. Lawyers for the BBC had complained that Trump was delaying his appearance in his own lawsuit. Charles Tobin, an attorney for the BBC , said that with two months left in the discovery period, “we still haven’t been able to depose the plaintiff.” The deposition deadline could yet be extended.
Trump called Kuntz’s latest ruling a major victory.

“A Huge Victory against Fake News BBC, a terrible abuser of the truth, just handed down by highly respected District Court Judge, Jeffrey T. Kuntz, of the Southern District of Florida,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.
“We will continue fighting against, and defeating, all of those who try to deceive the American People!” Trump wrote Tuesday evening.

title_en: ‘Draft Marco’ effort grows on Capitol Hill after midterms bloodbath
title_zh: 中期选举大屠杀后，国会山的“马可草案”努力不断加强
summary: More and more Republicans see a wide open 2028 presidential race — and are eyeing Marco Rubio.
summary_zh: 越来越多的共和党人看到了 2028 年总统竞选的开放性，并且将目光投向了马可·卢比奥。
body_en: A growing number of Republicans on Capitol Hill want to draft Marco Rubio for a 2028 presidential bid as they grapple with their midterms wipeout — and look beyond Vice President JD Vance.

The generational losses are sparking new discussions among Hill Republicans about who should lead the party. Many argue the race to carry the mantle is now wide open — including a faction who view Rubio as a better fit, given that voters may continue to tie Vance to the president’s unpopularity, interviews with roughly two dozen GOP lawmakers reveal.
“I hope he runs. I think he's the best person to communicate, to unify,” Rep. Marlin Stutzman (R-Ind.) said of Rubio in an interview.

“I think he's the most talented Republican by far,” Stutzman said when asked about why he supported the secretary of State over Vance. “We're going to have to continue to re-message, put some new faces up.” The vice president still has his supporters. And he got a boost Tuesday by fellow Ohio Republican Jim Jordan being elected as the incoming House minority leader.
But the election wipeout “certainly makes it harder for Vance,” said one GOP senator, who like others in this article, was granted anonymity to speak candidly.
“I think Rubio is our best hope to lead Republicans out of this wilderness, and I hope he makes his break from Trump and JD early next year,” said one House Republican in the wake of the election.

The openness toward Rubio — or any other candidate that’s not Vance — is a complication for the vice president, who was picked by Trump for the role that’s next in line to the presidency. Now, Vance has to grapple with being closely associated with an agenda that even GOP lawmakers argue voters harshly rebuked last week.

Several lawmakers said they’ve spoken to people close to Rubio who have suggested he isn’t interested in pursuing a 2028 bid, even after Tuesday’s results. Rubio himself this week has stood by Trump’s decision to go to war against Iran and told reporters Monday he was “just not going to talk about 2028 anymore.”

A person close to Rubio said the secretary of State is the only person who knows what he will do regarding a presidential bid. Right now, he’s “fully focused on doing his many jobs and isn’t thinking about 2028.”
But some Hill Republicans aren’t giving up hope.

“I’m a big supporter of Marco Rubio, and I’m very excited about the potential of his candidacy,” said Florida Rep. Mike Haridopolos, who has known the secretary of State for nearly three decades. “No question he’s ready to be president if he chooses to pursue the office.”
“Some of us are still hoping we can draft Marco,” said another GOP senator.
A State Department spokesperson declined to comment. Vance’s office didn’t respond to a request for comment.

In reaction to Stutzman’s comments, a Vance ally argued that Stutzman has been one of the biggest supporters within the GOP of amnesty for unauthorized immigrants for over a decade — and that he was likely never going to support Vance, who is extremely hawkish on border security.

Vance, for his part, has tried to distance himself from the unpopular Iran war, blaming it for the party’s losses in the immediate aftermath of the midterm election. His allies argue that the vice president would’ve always faced some internal opposition, like Trump did within the GOP ahead of the 2016 election.

However, as the Rubio talk swirls, even some of Trump’s top MAGA allies on Capitol Hill are unwilling to publicly declare Vance the presumptive GOP nominee for 2028. “Can I skip this one?” one House GOP hardliner said. “Not wading into 2028 yet.” Some Republican senators also declined to back Vance just yet, citing their own reelections.
GOP Rep. and Sen.-elect Barry Moore of Alabama said he thought Vance would certainly “have a shot” at the presidency in 2028. Moore was the first member of Congress to back Trump for the 2016 race.
But Moore for now is leaving his endorsement up in the air: “We got a great bench," he said. "Whoever steps up, we'll be happy to support.”

Rubio’s supporters say that he’s not as closely associated with the 2026 GOP wipeout as Vance, but he could face his own obstacles. Rubio, unlike Vance, has continued to show strong support for the war in Iran, a conflict he’s tied to as the country’s top diplomat. Some GOP lawmakers have also grown frustrated with the amount of information the Trump administration, including Rubio at times, has been willing to share about the ongoing conflict.
Rubio also has his failed 2016 presidential run to contend with, including an infamous debate performance where he awkwardly repeated the same rehearsed line multiple times.
body_zh: 国会山越来越多的共和党人希望起草马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 参加 2028 年总统竞选，因为他们正在努力应对中期选举的惨败，而且他们的目光超越了副总统 JD 万斯 (JD Vance)。
代际损失正在引发希尔共和党人关于谁应该领导该党的新讨论。许多人认为，接任总统的竞选现在已经展开——其中包括一个派系，他们认为卢比奥更适合，因为选民可能会继续将万斯与总统不受欢迎联系起来，对大约两打共和党议员的采访显示。
“我希望他参选。我认为他是沟通、团结的最佳人选，”众议员马林·斯塔茨曼（印第安纳州共和党人）在接受采访时谈到卢比奥时说道。
“我认为他是迄今为止最有才华的共和党人，”当被问及为什么他支持国务卿而不是万斯时，斯图茨曼说道。 “我们将不得不继续重新发布信息，发布一些新面孔。”副总统仍然有他的支持者。周二，俄亥俄州共和党人吉姆·乔丹当选为即将上任的众议院少数党领袖，这让他得到了提振。
但选举的惨败“肯定让万斯的处境变得更加困难”，一位共和党参议员说，他和本文中的其他人一样，被允许匿名坦率地发言。
一位众议院共和党人在选举后表示：“我认为卢比奥是我们带领共和党走出这片荒野的最大希望，我希望他明年初摆脱特朗普和 JD。”
对卢比奥或除万斯以外的任何其他候选人的开放态度对于副总统来说是一个复杂的问题，他被特朗普选为下一任总统。现在，万斯必须努力与一项议程密切相关，就连共和党议员也认为选民上周严厉谴责了这一议程。
几位议员表示，他们已经与卢比奥关系密切的人士进行了交谈，他们表示，即使在周二的选举结果公布之后，卢比奥也没有兴趣参加 2028 年的竞选。卢比奥本人本周坚持特朗普对伊朗开战的决定，并于周一告诉记者，他“只是不再谈论 2028 年”。
一位与卢比奥关系密切的人士表示，国务卿是唯一知道他将在总统竞选中做什么的人。目前，他“完全专注于完成自己的多项工作，没有考虑 2028 年的情况”。
但一些希尔共和党人并没有放弃希望。
“我是马可·卢比奥的坚定支持者，我对他的候选资格感到非常兴奋，”与国务卿相识近三十年的佛罗里达州众议员迈克·哈里多波洛斯说。 “毫无疑问，如果他选择竞选总统，他就已经准备好担任总统了。”
另一位共和党参议员表示：“我们中的一些人仍然希望能够选中马可。”
美国国务院发言人拒绝置评。万斯的办公室没有回应置评请求。
作为对斯图茨曼言论的回应，万斯的一位盟友辩称，十多年来，斯图茨曼一直是共和党内大赦非法移民的最大支持者之一，而且他很可能永远不会支持在边境安全问题上极其强硬的万斯。
万斯则试图与不受欢迎的伊朗战争保持距离，将中期选举后该党的失利归咎于这场战争。他的盟友认为，副总统总是会面临一些内部反对，就像特朗普在 2016 年大选前在共和党内部所做的那样。
然而，随着卢比奥言论的不断发酵，即使是特朗普在国会山的一些顶级盟友也不愿意公开宣布万斯成为共和党 2028 年的推定提名人。“我可以跳过这个吗？”一位众议院共和党强硬派表示。 “还没有进入 2028 年。”一些共和党参议员也以自己的连任为由拒绝支持万斯。
阿拉巴马州共和党众议员和当选参议员巴里·摩尔表示，他认为万斯肯定“有机会”担任 2028 年总统职位。摩尔是第一位支持特朗普参加 2016 年竞选的国会议员。
但摩尔目前对他的支持仍悬而未决：“我们有一个很棒的板凳，”他说。 “无论谁挺身而出，我们都会很乐意提供支持。”
卢比奥的支持者表示，他不像万斯那样与 2026 年共和党被淘汰的关系密切，但他也可能面临自己的障碍。与万斯不同，卢比奥继续对伊朗战争表示强烈支持，他作为该国最高外交官与这场冲突息息相关。一些共和党议员也对特朗普政府（包括卢比奥有时）愿意分享有关持续冲突的大量信息感到沮丧。
卢比奥还面临着 2016 年总统竞选失败的问题，其中包括一次臭名昭著的辩论表演，他多次笨拙地重复排练过的同一句话。

title_en: Marco Rubio reportedly spent over $1.2m of taxpayer money traveling to son’s football games
title_zh: 据报道，马可·卢比奥花费了超过 120 万美元的纳税人钱去看儿子的足球比赛
summary: Ethics watchdogs question necessity of the US secretary of state flying between DC and Gainesville so often Marco Rubio , the US secretary of state, has emerged as a superfan of the University of Florida ’s football team, spending more than $1.2m of taxpayers’
summary_zh: 道德监管机构质疑美国国务卿频繁往返于华盛顿特区和盖恩斯维尔之间的必要性 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio)
body_en: Ethics watchdogs question necessity of the US secretary of state flying between DC and Gainesville so often

Marco Rubio , the US secretary of state, has emerged as a superfan of the University of Florida ’s football team, spending more than $1.2m of taxpayers’ money on frequent personal trips to watch them play, a report published on Wednesday claims.

Ethics watchdogs have questioned the necessity of the country’s top diplomat shuttling so often between Washington DC and Gainesville, where his son Anthony has a walk-on role as a running back for the team known as the Gators.

An investigation by the Washington Post found that Rubio has attended at least 10 games in the last two seasons, including five this fall, and that of 23 total trips made to Gainesville on military aircraft, 15 were “personal” in nature.

The newspaper said that while Rubio is prohibited from flying commercially, because of security protocols that also cover the secretary of defense and FBI and CIA directors, his use of government transport “appears to significantly outpace that of his predecessors”.
Using published defense department rates listing the cost per hour of different kinds of military aircraft, the Post calculated that the flights alone have cost more than $1.2m.

Most recently, on 7 November, Rubio arrived in Gainesville on board an Air Force C-37, a plane used frequently for the VIP transport of high-ranking government officials, and was seen on the sidelines as the Gators lost 23-7 to Oklahoma. Anthony Rubio played no part in the game.

Rubio, in a statement to the Post, defended his prolific trips to Florida , which often feature flights from Joint Base Andrews in Maryland to the Homestead Air Reserve Base near Miami, and a secondary flight from there to Gainesville.
“I have and will continue to try and make it to as many events that are important to me personally and to my family as possible,” he said.

Statistics, however, show that Anthony Rubio, a senior and the third of his four children, has played in only four competitive games in his four years at the university, two of them this season. According to ESPN , he has a college career total of 14 carries for a combined total of 75 yards, and a single touchdown.

Officials who use military transport are required to reimburse the government the equivalent of an economy-fare ticket for their travel, which in every case would be far exceeded by the real cost of the journey.
Rubio and the state department declined to say how much he has reimbursed the public purse, the Post said.

Cynthia Brown, senior ethics counsel at the nonpartisan watchdog Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (Crew), told the Post that Rubio’s travel appeared “more of an optics issue than a violation”, but said it merited further scrutiny.
“If this travel becomes something that is undermining the integrity of your service, are you really taking care of taxpayer dollars the way that you’re obligated to as a public official?” she said.

“It is something that I think is really important to shine the light on.”
Brown noted that while Rubio might not be doing anything that is “technically improper”, he is the sole arbiter of how often and how far he travels.
The Post, citing two former government officials, reported that Antony Blinken, who was Joe Biden’s secretary of state, took personal trips on government aircraft “only a couple of times a year”.

Another Biden official, then transportation secretary Pete Buttigieg, was investigated by the department’s internal watchdog for his use of government jets for personal trips after a complaint by Rubio , who was the Republican senator for Florida at the time.
body_zh: 道德监管机构质疑美国国务卿频繁往返于华盛顿和盖恩斯维尔之间的必要性
周三发布的一份报告称，美国国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) 已成为佛罗里达大学橄榄球队的超级粉丝，他花费超过 120 万美元纳税人的钱经常亲自出差观看球队比赛。
道德监管机构质疑该国最高外交官如此频繁地往返于华盛顿特区和盖恩斯维尔之间的必要性，他的儿子安东尼在盖恩斯维尔担任鳄鱼队的跑卫。
《华盛顿邮报》的一项调查发现，卢比奥在过去两个赛季至少观看了 10 场比赛，其中包括今年秋天的 5 场，而在乘坐军用飞机前往盖恩斯维尔的 23 次旅行中，有 15 次是“私人”性质的。
该报称，虽然卢比奥被禁止乘坐商业航班，但由于安全协议也涵盖国防部长、联邦调查局和中央情报局局长，他对政府交通工具的使用“似乎大大超过了他的前任”。
根据公布的国防部公布的不同类型军用飞机每小时成本的费率，《华盛顿邮报》计算出仅这些航班的成本就超过 120 万美元。
最近的一次是在 11 月 7 日，卢比奥乘坐空军 C-37 飞机抵达盖恩斯维尔，这架飞机经常用于政府高级官员的 VIP 运输，在鳄鱼队以 23-7 输给俄克拉荷马州的比赛中，卢比奥在场边被看到。安东尼·卢比奥没有参加比赛。
卢比奥在给《华盛顿邮报》的一份声明中为自己多次前往佛罗里达州的旅行进行了辩护，这些旅行通常包括从马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地飞往迈阿密附近的霍姆斯特德空军储备基地的航班，以及从那里飞往盖恩斯维尔的二次航班。
“我已经并将继续尝试参加尽可能多的对我个人和我的家人来说很重要的活动，”他说。
然而，统计数据显示，安东尼·卢比奥是一名大四学生，也是他四个孩子中的第三个，他在大学的四年里只参加了四场正式比赛，其中两场是本赛季。据 ESPN 报道，他大学生涯共 14 次冲球，总推进 75 码，并有一次达阵。
使用军事交通工具的官员必须向政府报销相当于经济舱机票的旅行费用，而在任何情况下，这都远远超过实际旅行费用。
《华盛顿邮报》称，卢比奥和国务院拒绝透露他偿还了多少公共资金。
华盛顿无党派监督机构公民责任与道德组织 (Crew) 的高级道德顾问辛西娅·布朗 (Cynthia Brown) 告诉《华盛顿邮报》，卢比奥的旅行似乎“更像是一个光学问题，而不是违规行为”，但表示这值得进一步审查。
“如果这次旅行成为破坏你服务诚信的事情，你是否真的按照作为公职人员的义务来照顾纳税人的钱？”她说。
卢比奥告诉古巴人“现在是时候”采取行动实现政治变革
“我认为，照亮这一点非常重要。”
布朗指出，虽然卢比奥可能没有做任何“技术上不当”的事情，但他是他出行频率和距离的唯一仲裁者。
《华盛顿邮报》援引两名前政府官员的话说，乔·拜登的国务卿安东尼·布林肯“每年只乘坐政府飞机几次”。
另一名拜登官员、时任交通部长皮特·布蒂吉格(Pete Buttigieg)在时任佛罗里达州共和党参议员卢比奥的投诉后，因使用政府飞机进行私人旅行而受到该部门内部监管机构的调查。

title_en: What's behind democratic socialists' historic victories in the midterms?
title_zh: 民主社会主义者在中期选举中取得历史性胜利的背后是什么？
summary: Historian and The New Yorker writer Jill Lepore says the DSA, once maligned, is no longer "beyond the political pale." She discusses the history of socialism in America, and its current resurgence.
summary_zh: 历史学家兼《纽约客》作家吉尔·莱波雷 (Jill Lepore) 表示，一度饱受诟病的 DSA 已不再“超越政治范围”。她讨论了这样的历史
body_en: What’s behind democratic socialists' historic victories in the midterms? Historian and The New Yorker writer Jill Lepore says the DSA, once maligned, is no longer "beyond the political pale." She discusses the history of socialism in America, and its current resurgence.

Historian and The New Yorker writer Jill Lepore says the DSA, once maligned, is no longer "beyond the political pale." She discusses the history of socialism in America, and its current resurgence.

This is FRESH AIR. I'm Terry Gross. American socialists are having their best year since 1912. In last week's midterms, six socialists were elected to Congress, and three were elected mayor, which means New York, LA, Washington, D.C., Seattle, Ann Arbor and Providence, Rhode Island, are now led by socialists. But socialism means different things to different people. Even among American socialists, then and now, different factions have serious disagreements over what the agenda should be.

My guest, Jill Lepore, has written about the history of American socialism from the founding of the Socialist Party of America in 1901 to today's DSA, Democratic Socialists of America. Her new article in The New Yorker is titled "Can American Socialism Survive Its Success?" She's also recently written about whether the president has the power to declare war and how difficult it is to be a historian in a period when President Donald Trump is trying to rewrite American history and deleting its darker parts in schools, national parks and museums.

Lepore is a professor of American history at Harvard University, professor of law at Harvard Law School and a staff writer at The New Yorker. Her books include The New York Times bestsellers "These Truths: A History Of The United States" and "We The People: A History Of The U.S. Constitution," which won a 2026 Pulitzer Prize. Her latest, "The Rise And Fall Of The Artificial State," is about how AI is affecting politics and government.
JILL LEPORE: Hey. thanks so much for having me, Terry.

GROSS: My pleasure. Socialism means different things to different people, and there are different factions within the DSA that define socialism differently. So let's look at the national DSA and its positions, and then we'll talk about what other people in local branches of the DSA have to say. So Megan Romer, the co-chair of national DSA, was asked about the official national agenda in an interview on the "Fox News Sunday" show with Shannon Bream. So this was broadcast on July 26. So let's hear an excerpt of that interview.
SHANNON BREAM: OK. So we're going to put up on the screen a few of the things that are part of your platform, and I want to ask you - just give me sort of a true/false on these. Abolish the Senate.
BREAM: OK. Replace the presidency and Supreme Court as we now know them.
BREAM: Abolish borders and give amnesty to anyone currently in the U.S. illegally.
BREAM: Abolish prisons, at least in large part.
ROMER: Yeah, again, as part of a long-term program. Yeah.
BREAM: OK, so no prisons. Government or public ownership of most large corporations.
GROSS: So, Jill Lepore, that sounds very extreme.

LEPORE: Yeah, I mean, it was a notorious interview, too, and listening to the audio really comes across why. I mean, the format, the quiz, doesn't serve Megan Romer well, but it's her tone of voice and giving answers that are, you know, certifying that these are the formal positions of the platform of the DSA is quite glib. There's a little bit of kind of an edge of laughter there that I think exacerbated the perception of the extremism of the DSA.

GROSS: Do you want to explain a couple of things on that agenda that might make sense if you knew what they were about? Like, let's start with abolishing the Senate. That actually goes back a long way. And the Senate was a compromise in the Constitution.

LEPORE: Really, that's actually one of the more mainstream positions on that platform. I absolutely understand that it comes across as extreme. But there is a long tradition of calling for the abolition of the Senate, and it's not entirely a socialist position. So, you know, I was really immediately struck watching that interview how many of those items on the to-do list were on the 1912 formal platform of the Socialist Party of America, which was a political party. DSA is not a political party.
body_zh: 民主社会主义者在中期选举中取得历史性胜利的背后是什么？历史学家兼《纽约客》作家吉尔·莱波雷 (Jill Lepore) 表示，一度饱受诟病的 DSA 已不再“超越政治范围”。她讨论了美国社会主义的历史及其当前的复兴。
您的支持有助于我们的演出成为可能，并解锁我们的无赞助商动态。
历史学家兼《纽约客》作家吉尔·莱波雷 (Jill Lepore) 表示，一度饱受诟病的 DSA 已不再“超越政治范围”。她讨论了美国社会主义的历史及其当前的复兴。
这是新鲜空气。我是特里·格罗斯。美国社会主义者正迎来自1912年以来最好的一年。在上周的中期选举中，六名社会主义者当选国会议员，三人当选市长，这意味着纽约、洛杉矶、华盛顿特区、西雅图、安娜堡和罗德岛州普罗维登斯现在由社会主义者领导。但社会主义对不同的人有不同的含义。即使在当时和现在的美国社会主义者中，不同派系对于议程应该是什么也存在严重分歧。
我的客人 Jill Lepore 撰写了有关美国社会主义历史的文章，从 1901 年美国社会党成立到今天的 DSA（美国民主社会主义者）。她在《纽约客》上发表的新文章题为“美国社会主义能否成功？”她最近还撰写了有关总统是否有权宣战的文章，以及在唐纳德·特朗普总统试图改写美国历史并删除学校、国家公园和博物馆中的黑暗部分的时期，成为一名历史学家是多么困难。
莱波雷是哈佛大学美国历史教授、哈佛法学院法学教授和《纽约客》特约撰稿人。她的著作包括《纽约时报》畅销书《这些真理：美国历史》和《我们人民：美国宪法史》，该书荣获 2026 年普利策奖。她的最新作品《人工国家的兴衰》讲述了人工智能如何影响政治和政府。
吉尔·莱波雷：嘿。非常感谢你邀请我，特里。

格罗斯：我的荣幸。社会主义对不同的人有不同的含义，DSA 内部也有不同的派别，对社会主义有不同的定义。因此，让我们看看国家 DSA 及其立场，然后我们将讨论 DSA 地方分支机构的其他人员的看法。因此，国家 DSA 联合主席梅根·罗默 (Megan Romer) 在接受《福克斯周日新闻》节目采访香农·布里姆 (Shannon Bream) 时被问及官方国家议程。这是 7 月 26 日播出的。让我们听听采访的摘录。
香农·布里姆：好的。因此，我们将在屏幕上显示一些属于您平台一部分的内容，我想问您 - 请给我对这些内容的正确/错误判断。废除参议院。
布里姆：好的。取代我们现在所知道的总统和最高法院。
布雷姆：废除边界，并特赦目前在美国非法居留的任何人。
布雷姆：废除监狱，至少在很大程度上。
ROMER：是的，再次，作为长期计划的一部分。是的。
布里姆：好的，所以没有监狱。大多数大公司为政府或公共所有。
格罗斯：吉尔·莱波雷（Jill Lepore），这听起来非常极端。
LEPORE：是的，我的意思是，这也是一次臭名昭著的采访，听音频才真正明白为什么。我的意思是，这种形式、测验对梅根·罗默来说不太好，但她的语气和给出的答案，你知道，证明这些是 DSA 平台的正式立场，这是相当油腔滑调的。我认为那里有一点笑声，这加剧了人们对 DSA 极端主义的看法。
格罗斯：你想解释一下议程上的一些事情吗？如果你知道它们的内容，这些事情可能会有意义吗？就像，让我们从废除参议院开始。这实际上可以追溯到很久以前。参议院是对宪法的妥协。
LEPORE：确实，这实际上是该平台上更主流的立场之一。我完全理解这听起来很极端。但要求废除参议院的传统由来已久，而且这并不完全是社会主义立场。所以，你知道，当我看到那次采访时，我立即感到震惊，因为待办事项清单上有多少项目出现在美国社会党（一个政党）1912 年的正式纲领上。 DSA 不是一个政党。

title_en: Several Dem women leaned into their identity this cycle. Not in the way you think.
title_zh: 几位民主党女性在这个周期中倾向于自己的身份。不是你想的那样。
summary: They focused less on the historic nature of their bids and more on parenting in a tough economy.
summary_zh: 他们较少关注投标的历史性质，而更多地关注在经济困难时期的养育问题。
body_en: When Annie Andrews announced her longshot campaign for U.S. Senate last May, the Democrat from South Carolina pitched herself as a “busy mom.”

“Lindsey [Graham] is going to tell you I am radical, that I am crazy,” Andrews said in her launch video . “But here’s the thing: I am literally a busy mom and a pediatrician who plays peek-a-boo with my patients, watches Bluey with my kids … and spends most of my free time shuttling them to dance, Tae Kwon Do and football.”

Now, she is one of a record number of women who will serve in the next Congress. And as a 46-year-old mother of three school-aged children, she’s among several Democratic women who flipped seats and governor’s mansions this November with campaign messages centered on parenting and affordability.

It’s a notable campaign shift from previous election cycles: This year, female candidates focused less on the historic nature of their bids, or culture war issues that have long fomented divisions over gender and electability. Instead, they zeroed in on an economic message emphasizing bread-and-butter concerns — like how rising costs were squeezing families, including theirs.

“Moms understand kitchen table issues better than perhaps anyone,” said Jessica Mackler, president of EMILY’s List, the group that recruits and backs female Democratic candidates who support abortion rights. “They understand how to stretch a paycheck. They understand what it is like to walk through a grocery store and have to put something back on the shelf.”

Senate, House and gubernatorial campaigns spent a combined $72 million on ads featuring the words “mom” or “mother” in 2026, according to AdImpact — a 50% increase from the $48 million spent in 2024 and double the spending on these kind of ads from 2022.
In many races, Democrats leaned on their experiences as parents to dismiss the kind of culture war attacks that have been effective for Republicans in recent years.

“They want to run an entire campaign saying that I’m too woke … I plan to spend an entire campaign focused on the fact that working people are too broke,” Democratic Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa said in one of her final TV ads . “My pronouns are mom, Texan and soon-to-be governor.”

Campaign messaging around gender and representation can be fraught: In 2016, Hillary Clinton’s “I’m With Her” campaign slogan fell short as she failed in her pledge to break the “highest, hardest glass ceiling.” In 2024, Kamala Harris’ campaign was decidedly less overt in its messaging about the barrier-breaking potential of her candidacy. But debates about gender seemed inescapable as Trump called her “weak” and then-Sen. JD Vance said the Democratic Party was run by “childless cat ladies.”

In a 2026 environment driven by concerns about affordability and the cost of living, Democratic operatives said it was an easy decision for women and mothers in particular to lean on their home lives to connect with voters.

At least 159 women will serve in the 120th Congress, according to the Center for American Women and Politics, with Democratic women outnumbering Republicans by roughly five-to-one. Many of the newly elected Democrats are younger moms.

Their victories, especially in battleground districts and states long seen as Republican strongholds, have emboldened Democratic groups dedicated to electing more women, who argue the candidates offer a blueprint for winning races going forward.
Veteran Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said her party’s female candidates “really got points for having the right priorities and being in touch with real people's lives."

"It used to be that women with young children just didn't run, and we were electing all these women who had grown children or no children, and then we were electing women with young children, but they were hiding them, if you will,” Lake said. “Now [candidates] were bringing them out as major credentialers, and that has been changing over time."
Winning Democratic candidates told POLITICO they did not hesitate to talk about their families and personal experiences on the trail.

“I didn’t need anyone giving me talking points on how expensive groceries are,” said Representative-elect Teresa Benitez-Thompson, who won a heavily Republican House district in northern Nevada. “I don’t need anyone telling me how expensive gas is because I am filling up my tank … running kids all around town.”
JoAnna Mendoza, a single mom who flipped a swing district in the Tucson, Arizona, suburbs – said she spent the night before the election in the emergency room with her 10-year-old son.

“That is what parents face. That is what moms go through. Their kids are sick, they have to take time off of work, or they have to leave work,” Mendoza said. “It is important for people to see themselves in their elected leaders.”

Uncomfortable questions surrounding gender and electability nevertheless persist in the run-up to the next presidential election. Some in the Democratic Party at least privately question whether they should nominate another woman at the top of the ticket in 2028.

“My message to people who would say that is: cut it out,” said Mackler. “This election clearly demonstrates that women are the drivers of Democrats' path to power, and we should embrace their leadership at all levels of the ballot.”
body_zh: 去年五月，当安妮·安德鲁斯 (Annie Andrews) 宣布竞选美国参议员的希望渺茫时，这位来自南卡罗来纳州的民主党人将自己定位为“忙碌的妈妈”。
“林赛（格雷厄姆）会告诉你我很激进，我很疯狂，”安德鲁斯在她的发布视频中说道。 “但事情是这样的：我实际上是一个忙碌的妈妈和一名儿科医生，我和我的病人一起玩躲猫猫，和我的孩子们一起看《Bluey》……我大部分的空闲时间都花在送他们去跳舞、踢跆拳道和踢足球。”
现在，她是在下一届国会任职的女性人数创纪录的一员。作为一名 46 岁的三个学龄儿童的母亲，她是今年 11 月推翻席位和州长官邸的几位民主党女性之一，她们的竞选信息以育儿和负担能力为中心。
与之前的选举周期相比，这是一个显着的竞选转变：今年，女性候选人较少关注其竞选的历史性质，或长期以来引发性别和选举分歧的文化战争问题。相反，他们把注意力集中在强调生计问题的经济信息上——比如成本上涨如何挤压家庭，包括他们自己的家庭。
“妈妈们可能比任何人都更了解厨房餐桌问题，”艾米莉名单主席杰西卡·麦克勒说，该组织招募和支持支持堕胎权的女性民主党候选人。 “他们了解如何延长薪水。他们了解走进杂货店并必须将某些东西放回货架上是什么感觉。”
根据 AdImpact 的数据，2026 年，参议院、众议院和州长竞选活动在带有“妈妈”一词的广告上总共花费了 7200 万美元，比 2024 年的 4800 万美元增加了 50%，比 2022 年此类广告的支出增加了一倍。
在许多竞选中，民主党人依靠自己作为父母的经历来驳回近年来对共和党人有效的文化战争攻击。
“他们想要开展整个竞选活动，说我太清醒了……我计划用整个竞选活动来关注劳动人民太破产这一事实，”民主党德克萨斯州州长当选人吉娜·伊诺霍萨在她最后的电视广告中说道。 “我的代词是妈妈、德克萨斯人和即将成为州长的人。”

围绕性别和代表权的竞选信息可能会令人担忧：2016年，希拉里·克林顿(Hillary Clinton)的“我与她同在”竞选口号未能实现，因为她未能兑现打破“最高、最坚硬的玻璃天花板”的承诺。 2024 年，卡玛拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris) 的竞选活动在宣传她的候选资格突破障碍的潜力方面显然没有那么公开。但有关性别的争论似乎不可避免，因为特朗普称她“软弱”，而当时的参议员。 JD万斯称民主党是由“没有孩子的猫女士”管理的。
民主党工作人员表示，在 2026 年的环境下，人们对负担能力和生活成本感到担忧，依靠家庭生活与选民建立联系，对妇女和母亲来说是一个容易的决定。
据美国妇女与政治中心称，第 120 届国会将至少有 159 名女性任职，其中民主党女性人数与共和党女性人数之比约为五比一。许多新当选的民主党人都是年轻妈妈。
她们的胜利，尤其是在长期以来被视为共和党据点的战场地区和州的胜利，让致力于选举更多女性的民主党团体更加大胆，他们认为候选人为赢得未来的竞选提供了蓝图。
资深民主党民意调查专家塞琳达·莱克 (Celinda Lake) 表示，该党的女性候选人“确实因拥有正确的优先事项并接触真实人民的生活而获得加分。”
莱克说：“过去，有年幼孩子的女性不会参选，我们选举所有这些已经成年孩子或没有孩子的女性，然后我们选举有年幼孩子的女性，但如果你愿意的话，她们会隐藏孩子。” “现在（候选人）将他们作为主要资格认证者，这种情况随着时间的推移而发生了变化。”
获胜的民主党候选人告诉《政治》杂志，他们毫不犹豫地谈论了他们的家庭和个人经历。
“我不需要任何人给我关于食品杂货有多贵的谈话要点，”当选众议员特雷莎·贝尼特斯·汤普森说，她赢得了内华达州北部共和党占多数的众议院选区。 “我不需要任何人告诉我汽油有多贵，因为我正在加满油……带着孩子们在城里跑来跑去。”
乔安娜·门多萨 (JoAnna Mendoza) 是一位单亲妈妈，她在亚利桑那州图森市郊区的一个摇摆区工作。她说，选举前一天晚上，她和 10 岁的儿子在急诊室度过。
“这就是父母所面临的。这就是妈妈们所经历的。他们的孩子生病了，他们必须请假，或者必须离开工作岗位，”门多萨说。 “人们在当选的领导人身上看到自己很重要。”
然而，在下届总统选举前夕，围绕性别和选举权的令人不安的问题仍然存在。民主党中的一些人至少私下质疑他们是否应该在 2028 年提名另一位女性候选人。
麦克勒说：“我要向那些持这种观点的人传达的信息是：别再这么说了。” “这次选举清楚地表明，女性是民主党掌权之路的推动者，我们应该拥抱她们在各级选举中的领导作用。”

title_en: Following big Democratic wins, these swing voters are looking for results
title_zh: 在民主党取得重大胜利后，这些摇摆选民正在寻找结果
summary: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.
summary_zh: 作为其 Swing Shift 系列的一部分，NPR 定期对摇摆选民进行调查，选举结果带来了复杂的情绪，钢笔也是如此。
body_en: Swing voters Theresa from Pennsylvania, Jason from North Carolina and Gerald from Georgia. All three voted in this year's midterms and all three have mixed emotions about the results. Tara Anand for NPR hide caption

Republicans were dealt a stunning rebuke in last week's midterms. But swing voters, who could be decisive in the next election, are more interested in results than investigations or impeachment as Democrats prepare to take power in Congress.

"I am hoping that we don't experience a bunch of gridlock and a lot of whining and crying and just political infighting for the next two years," said Theresa, a voter from Pennsylvania who is participating in NPR's Swing Shift project. "I'm hoping we don't have that. I fear that we will have that."
NPR has agreed not to use the full names of the Swing Shift voters, so they can speak freely about politics without fear of personal or professional repercussions.

Theresa voted for President Biden in 2020, President Trump in 2024 and split her ticket in this year's midterms. Like many voters, her top issue this year was affordability. In a voice memo sent to NPR days after the midterms, Theresa said she is eager for the cost of living to come down.
"I just don't remember it ever being as bad in our time," Theresa said. "And I'm just hoping we get some relief and we get some relief soon."
At 9:56 PM on election night, Wally in Georgia hit send on his voice memo. He had seen enough.

"Just checking in here with a quick note. I'm not surprised at all by the outcome tonight," Wally said. "I believe that this is a lot of Trump's doing and pushback on his style of politics and how he governs."

Wally voted for Trump in 2024 but swung back to Democrats in this year's midterms. He had initially supported Trump in hopes that a Trump presidency would shake up the political system, but that didn't happen and now he says the second Trump term has been exhausting. As he sees it, the decisive Democratic wins signal that the country is ready to move on.
The Democratic Party gained power across the country in the midterms. Now what?

"Trump has been shooting himself in the foot for many months now," Wally said. "But voting isn't the end of the game here. We have to hold Democrats to some sort of tangible change and not just promises about what they want to do."
For several of the Swing Shift voters, Tuesday's results came as a surprise.
Jason from North Carolina split his ticket, voting for Democrat Roy Cooper for Senate and the Republican incumbent for the House.
"My congressman was defeated this time by someone that no one's really ever heard of," said Jason, sounding almost puzzled by the blue wave that crashed on North Carolina.
That happened in a lot of places. Jason wants the incoming Democratic Congress to focus on the cost of living and steer clear of impeachment.
"My fear is that the Democrats now are going to spend the next 2 years not focusing on any of the things that they say Trump didn't do," said Jason.
Michelle in Michigan, voted for President Biden in 2020 but chose Republicans in 2024 and again in this year's midterms.
"This is the first time I think ever since I've been voting that not one of the people that I voted for won their election," Michelle said.

Michelle says she understands why so many people voted for Democrats, even if she didn't. Americans are tired, she said, of high gas prices, the cost of living and not being able to afford their groceries. They voted for change.
body_zh: 来自宾夕法尼亚州的摇摆选民特蕾莎、来自北卡罗来纳州的杰森和来自佐治亚州的杰拉德。三人都在今年的中期选举中投票，三人对结果都有复杂的情绪。 NPR 的塔拉·阿南德隐藏标题栏
共和党人在上周的中期选举中遭到了令人震惊的指责。但随着民主党准备在国会掌权，摇摆选民可能在下次选举中发挥决定性作用，他们对结果更感兴趣，而不是调查或弹劾。
“我希望未来两年我们不会经历一系列的僵局、大量的牢骚和哭泣以及政治内斗，”参与 NPR 摇摆转变项目的宾夕法尼亚州选民特蕾莎说。 “我希望我们不会有这样的事。我担心我们会有这样的事。”
NPR 已同意不使用 Swing Shift 选民的全名，以便他们可以自由谈论政治，而不必担心个人或职业影响。
特蕾莎在 2020 年投票给拜登总统，在 2024 年投票给特朗普总统，并在今年的中期选举中平分了选票。和许多选民一样，她今年最关心的问题是负担能力。在中期选举几天后发送给美国国家公共广播电台的语音备忘录中，特蕾莎表示她渴望生活成本下降。
特蕾莎说：“我不记得我们这个时代的情况有这么糟糕过。” “我只是希望我们能得到一些缓解，并且很快就能得到一些缓解。”
选举之夜晚上 9 点 56 分，佐治亚州的沃利按下了语音备忘录上的“发送”键。他已经看够了。
“只是在这里简单记录一下。我对今晚的结果一点也不感到惊讶，”沃利说。 “我相信这是特朗普的很多做法，也是对他的政治风格和执政方式的抵制。”
沃利在 2024 年投票支持特朗普，但在今年的中期选举中又转回民主党。他最初支持特朗普，希望特朗普当选总统后能够撼动政治体系，但这并没有发生，现在他说特朗普的第二个任期已经让人筋疲力尽。在他看来，民主党的决定性胜利表明该国已准备好继续前进。
民主党在中期选举中在全国获得了权力。现在怎么办？
沃利说：“几个月来，特朗普一直在搬起石头砸自己的脚。” “但投票并不是游戏的终点。我们必须让民主党做出某种切实的改变，而不仅仅是承诺他们想做的事情。”
对于一些摇摆轮班选民来说，周二的结果令人惊讶。
来自北卡罗来纳州的杰森将他的选票分开，投票给民主党参议员罗伊·库珀和共和党众议院议员。
“我的国会议员这次被一个没有人真正听说过的人击败了，”杰森说道，听起来对袭击北卡罗来纳州的蓝色浪潮感到困惑。
这种情况在很多地方都发生过。杰森希望即将上任的民主党国会关注生活成本并避免弹劾。
杰森说：“我担心民主党现在将在未来两年内不再关注他们所说的特朗普没有做过的任何事情。”
密歇根州的米歇尔在 2020 年投票支持拜登总统，但在 2024 年和今年的中期选举中再次选择了共和党。
米歇尔说：“自从我投票以来，这是我第一次认为我投票的人没有一个赢得选举。”
米歇尔说，她理解为什么这么多人投票给民主党，即使她没有。她说，美国人厌倦了高油价、高生活成本和买不起杂货。他们投票支持变革。

title_en: ‘A tremendous step backwards’: US could lose measles elimination status under RFK Jr’s leadership
title_zh: “巨大的倒退”：在小罗伯特·肯尼迪的领导下，美国可能会失去消除麻疹的地位
summary: Country is in the middle of worst measles outbreak since 1991, with more than 5,400 cases nationally The United States could lose its measles elimination status this week, an event likely to cement health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr’s legacy of meddling in
summary_zh: 该国正处于 1991 年以来最严重的麻疹疫情之中，全国已有 5,400 多例病例，美国可能会失去消除麻疹的机会
body_en: Country is in the middle of worst measles outbreak since 1991, with more than 5,400 cases nationally

The United States could lose its measles elimination status this week, an event likely to cement health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr’s legacy of meddling in vaccine policies amid the worst outbreak of the virus in the US in 35 years.
If the US loses its measles-free status, it would join Canada and several European and Asian nations that had eliminated the disease only for it to return.

“That is a tremendous step backwards,” said Dr Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center, an attending physician in the division of infectious diseases at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, and a prominent critic of Kennedy.

A panel of eight independent experts will consider the epidemiological evidence in Washington DC, part of a group called the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a regional branch of the World Health Organization (WHO). The PAHO director will make the final call.
The vaccine limbo in the US is worsening the measles outbreak

“Independent of what PAHO says, measles is now endemic in the US. Measles has a foothold in the US,” said Offit. “We’re going to see it this year, we’re going to see it next year,” because the US “critically decreased the percentage” of people vaccinated.

The US is in the midst of its worst measles outbreak since 1991 with more than 5,400 cases nationally, according to the Johns Hopkins University International Vaccine Access Center tracker. Just this year, six people have died in Pennsylvania, a child died in New York on election day and an infant died in Wisconsin days later. Nearly every US state has an active outbreak.

Measles is considered one of the most infectious diseases known to medicine. The overwhelming majority of Americans vaccinate themselves and their children, but the sheer contagiousness of measles means even small dips in immunity allow it to spread. It kills one to three people per 1,000 people and hospitalizes about one-in-five unvaccinated people who are infected. Two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is 97% effective against the disease.

Although elimination status is a formal public health designation, its loss has real effects on everyday Americans. In just one example, Dr David Margolius, the Cleveland, Ohio, director of public health, is warning people to find proof of their measles vaccination in the event they’re exposed to a measles-positive patient.

“Now is the time to go and find that evidence, because now this is a real day-to-day life thing that could happen to you,” said Margolius, who is also a director-at-large of the Big Cities Health Coalition. Without proof, patients face either an immunology blood draw or a 21-day quarantine.
Cleveland health authorities have already done a tremendous amount of detective work this year to track down people exposed to measles patients in hospital waiting rooms and elevators.

“We reach out to people and for most people, including myself, we have no personal experience with measles,” he said. “They’ve got everything else going on in their life, and now they’re getting this call.”

The types of people who contract measles has also changed. In 1963, when the vaccine was first licensed, measles was considered a childhood disease. Most children contracted the disease by the age of five.

“Now you’re seeing the epidemiology shift,” said Offit. Two-thirds of people infected with measles in Pennsylvania are adults, a group on which researchers have little information. Mothers have even given birth to babies with measles. “Now, you’re seeing something we just didn’t see at all – congenital measles.”

The potential loss of elimination status comes at a tenuous moment for the Trump administration. Republicans just endured a historic drubbing in the midterm elections. Several new Democratic doctors and scientists are slated to come into Congress on promises to hold Kennedy accountable . At the same time, Trump has doubled down on his commitment to vaccine antagonism with the appointment of Stephen Miller as chief of staff.
“Next to me, Stephen Miller is the strongest Maha supporter in the administration,” Kennedy said in a statement about Miller’s appointment. “It’s time to unleash the Kraken.”

Meanwhile, the capacity of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to respond has been significantly hampered by the Trump administration. The agency has lost up to one-third of its staff, Kennedy has interfered in the agency’s reporting of measles deaths and has spread misinformation about the measles vaccines .
Even so, Margolius doesn’t lay all the blame at Kennedy’s feet. Vaccine hesitancy was increasing before Trump took office, and pandemic-era disruptions were real.
body_zh: 该国正处于 1991 年以来最严重的麻疹疫情之中，全国已有 5,400 多例病例
美国本周可能会失去消除麻疹的地位，这一事件可能会巩固卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪在美国35年来最严重的病毒爆发期间干预疫苗政策的遗产。
如果美国失去无麻疹地位，它将加入加拿大和几个欧洲和亚洲国家的行列，消灭了这种疾病，但结果却又卷土重来。
“这是一个巨大的倒退，”疫苗教育中心主任、费城儿童医院传染病科主治医生、肯尼迪的著名批评者保罗·奥菲特博士说。
由八名独立专家组成的小组将考虑华盛顿特区的流行病学证据，该小组隶属于世界卫生组织（WHO）的区域分支机构泛美卫生组织（PAHO）。泛美卫生组织主任将做出最后决定。
美国的疫苗困境正在加剧麻疹疫情
“不管泛美卫生组织怎么说，麻疹现在在美国流行。麻疹在美国有立足之地，”奥菲特说。 “我们今年会看到这种情况，明年也会看到这种情况”，因为美国“大幅降低了”接种疫苗的人数。
根据约翰·霍普金斯大学国际疫苗获取中心追踪数据，美国正处于 1991 年以来最严重的麻疹疫情之中，全国已有 5,400 多例麻疹病例。就在今年，宾夕法尼亚州就有六人死亡，纽约州有一名儿童在选举日死亡，几天后威斯康星州有一名婴儿死亡。美国几乎每个州都爆发了活跃的疫情。
麻疹被认为是医学上已知的最具传染性的疾病之一。绝大多数美国人都会为自己和孩子接种疫苗，但麻疹的传染性很强，意味着即使免疫力的微小下降也会导致麻疹传播。每 1000 人中就有 1 到 3 人死亡，约五分之一的未接种疫苗的感染者需要住院治疗。两剂麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗对该疾病的有效率为 97%。
尽管消除状态是一个正式的公共卫生名称，但它的丧失对普通美国人产生了实际影响。仅举一个例子，俄亥俄州克利夫兰市公共卫生主任大卫·马戈利乌斯博士警告人们，如果接触到麻疹阳性患者，请寻找麻疹疫苗接种的证据。
“现在是时候去寻找证据了，因为现在这是可能发生在你身上的真实的日常生活事情，”同时也是大城市健康联盟的无任所长的马戈柳斯说。如果没有证据，患者要么面临免疫学抽血，要么面临 21 天的隔离。
克利夫兰卫生当局今年已经做了大量的侦探工作，以追踪在医院候诊室和电梯中接触过麻疹患者的人。
他说：“我们向人们伸出援手，对于包括我自己在内的大多数人来说，我们没有个人感染麻疹的经历。” “他们生活中的其他事情都在发生，现在他们接到了这个电话。”
感染麻疹的人的类型也发生了变化。 1963 年，当疫苗首次获得许可时，麻疹被认为是一种儿童疾病。大多数儿童在五岁时就感染了这种疾病。
“现在你看到了流行病学的转变，”奥菲特说。在宾夕法尼亚州，三分之二的麻疹感染者是成年人，研究人员对此群体的信息知之甚少。母亲们甚至生下患有麻疹的婴儿。 “现在，你看到了我们根本没有看到的东西——先天性麻疹。”
对于特朗普政府来说，可能失去淘汰地位正值微妙时刻。共和党刚刚在中期选举中遭受了历史性的惨败。几位新的民主党医生和科学家将进入国会，承诺追究肯尼迪的责任。与此同时，特朗普任命斯蒂芬·米勒为幕僚长，加大了对疫苗对抗的承诺。
“除了我之外，斯蒂芬·米勒是政府中最强有力的马哈支持者，”肯尼迪在一份关于米勒任命的声明中表示。 “是时候释放海妖了。”
与此同时，美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）的应对能力受到特朗普政府的严重阻碍。该机构已经失去了多达三分之一的员工，肯尼迪干预了该机构对麻疹死亡的报告，并散布了有关麻疹疫苗的错误信息。
即便如此，马戈留斯并没有将所有责任归咎于肯尼迪。在特朗普上任之前，人们对疫苗的犹豫不断增加，大流行时代的干扰是真实存在的。

title_en: Father charged with attempted murder after baby survives being buried in crate
title_zh: 婴儿被埋在板条箱中幸存，父亲被控谋杀未遂
summary: The father of an 11-month-old boy found alive after being buried in a dog crate has been charged with attempted murder and other counts, authorities said Wednesday.
summary_zh: 当局称，一名 11 个月大男孩被埋在狗笼里后被发现还活着，其父亲被指控谋杀未遂和其他罪名。
body_en: 11-month-old baby found safe after being buried alive
The father of an 11-month-old boy found alive after being buried in a dog crate has been charged with attempted murder and other counts, authorities said Wednesday.
The baby, Koah Sharp, was allegedly taken by his father, Michael Comer, 25, on Monday and the child was dug out of the ground Tuesday afternoon, the Lexington County, South Carolina, sheriff said.
The baby is expected to make a full recovery. He is believed to have been buried in the wire crate, which was wrapped in a towel for around 24 hours, Sheriff Brayn “Jay” Koon said.
The towel likely created an air pocket that allowed the Koah to breathe, and cool weather may have also helped the child to survive, Koon said.

Comer, who was arrested on a burglary charge after being found in an outbuilding Monday night, is charged with attempted murder, unlawful conduct toward a child, custodial interference and burglary, the sheriff’s office said Wednesday .
Searchers investigating a patch of disturbed earth near a home owned by Comer’s father heard the baby’s cries and quickly unearthed him, Koon said.
Koah was released from the hospital Tuesday, the sheriff’s office said, and the child is with family members.

The child was reported missing early Monday afternoon, authorities said. The report set off a search for the infant that included the FBI, firefighters, the federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and local law enforcement agencies.
Comer was in custody Wednesday, jail records showed. It was not immediately clear whether he had an attorney who could speak on his behalf.

Koah’s mother has custody of the child, Comer’s mother has said. The child’s mother told a sheriff’s deputy that she allowed Comer to briefly have the child but only expected that to last a day or two, according to a police report.
The mother told the deputy that Comer had threatened her over Facebook Messenger that he would keep the baby, according to the police report.
body_zh: 11个月大婴儿被活埋后被发现安全
当局周三表示，一名 11 个月大男孩被埋在狗笼中后被发现还活着，其父亲被指控谋杀未遂和其他罪名。
南卡罗来纳州列克星敦县治安官称，这名婴儿科阿·夏普 (Koah Sharp) 据称于周一被他 25 岁的父亲迈克尔·科默 (Michael Comer) 抱走，周二下午孩子被从地里挖出来。
预计婴儿将​​完全康复。警长布莱恩·“杰伊”·库恩 (Brayn “Jay” Koon) 表示，据信他被埋在铁丝箱中，并用毛巾包裹了大约 24 小时。
库恩说，毛巾可能形成了一个气穴，让科阿能够呼吸，凉爽的天气也可能帮助了孩子的生存。
治安官办公室周三表示，科默周一晚上在一栋附属建筑中被发现后，因入室盗窃罪被捕，他被指控犯有谋杀未遂、对儿童进行非法行为、干扰监护和入室盗窃等罪名。
库恩说，搜索人员在科默父亲的房屋附近调查一块被扰乱的土地时，听到了婴儿的哭声，很快就发现了他。
治安官办公室称，科阿于周二出院，孩子与家人在一起。
当局称，周一下午早些时候，据报道这名儿童失踪。该报告引发了对婴儿的搜查，包括联邦调查局、消防员、联邦烟酒枪械和爆炸物管理局以及当地执法机构。
监狱记录显示，科默于周三被拘留。目前尚不清楚他是否有律师可以代表他发言。
科默的母亲表示，科阿的母亲拥有孩子的监护权。据警方报告，孩子的母亲告诉副警长，她允许科默短暂生下孩子，但预计只持续一两天。
据警方报告称，这位母亲告诉警官，科默曾通过 Facebook Messenger 威胁她，称他会保留孩子。

title_en: Scott Colom ousts Cindy Hyde-Smith in historic Mississippi Senate flip
title_zh: 斯科特·科洛姆在历史性的密西西比州参议院翻转中驱逐辛迪·海德·史密斯
summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a stunning Mississippi upset , becoming the first Democrat elected to the state's Senate delegation since 1982, AP projects. Why it matters: Colom's victory marks another extraordinary breakthro
summary_zh: 民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 在令人震惊的密西西比州爆冷中击败了共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯 (Cindy Hyde-Smith)，成为第一位当选该州参议员的民主党人
body_en: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a stunning Mississippi upset , becoming the first Democrat elected to the state's Senate delegation since 1982, AP projects.
Why it matters: Colom's victory marks another extraordinary breakthrough for Democrats in the Deep South, extending the historic blue wave that handed the party control of both chambers of Congress.
Colom also becomes Mississippi's first Black senator since Reconstruction.
Hiram Rhodes Revels became the nation's first Black senator in 1870. Mississippi's last Black senator, Blanche K. Bruce, served until 1881.
Catch up quick: The race remained too close to call after Election Day, with Colom's victory expanding Democrats' 55–44 advantage over Republicans in the Senate.
The big picture: Colom's victory followed a late surge of Democratic spending and organizing in a state Trump carried by 23 points in 2024.
Hyde-Smith faced warning signs in the campaign's closing months, when Colom raised twice as much as the GOP senator despite her overall cash advantage.

She was also outspent on TV advertising , with a flood of ads from left-leaning PACs and super PACs pushing support for Colom and attacking the senator for her vote not to release files related to the convicted human trafficker Jeffrey Epstein.

Hyde-Smith's campaign also faced criticism over an interview she gave to WLOX-TV in Jackson, Mississippi, where she fumbled an answer about the price of beef, saying that Mississippians had "so many other proteins to choose from."
Colom's campaign capitalized on her blunder, creating a viral campaign ad urging voters to "choose another senator."
The GOP made a late push to help Hyde-Smith, including President Trump speaking at a rally for her in Alcorn County, where he won by 68% in 2024.
But it wasn't enough. Hyde-Smith's term will end after eight years.
She was appointed to the Senate in 2018 by then-Mississippi Gov. Phil Bryant, and ran for a full term in 2020, where she bested her Democratic challenger Mike Espy by 10 points.
Zoom in: Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney from Columbus, campaigned on lowering the cost of living, raising wages and protecting rural hospitals.
His campaign also drew in heavy Democratic hitters to stump for him, including former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock.
The bottom line: Colom's win adds Mississippi to a growing list of Republican strongholds where Democrats broke through in the midterms, including Texas and South Carolina.
It also reinforces the role of Black voters in the Democratic comeback, after the party rebuilt support among a crucial voting bloc that showed signs of shifting toward Trump in 2024.
body_zh: 据美联社报道，民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 在密西西比州令人震惊的爆冷中击败了共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯 (Cindy Hyde-Smith)，成为自 1982 年以来第一位当选该州参议院代表团的民主党人。
重要性：科罗姆的胜利标志着民主党在南方腹地的又一次非凡突破，延续了历史性的蓝色浪潮，该浪潮将国会两院的控制权交给了民主党。
科洛姆也成为密西西比州重建以来第一位黑人参议员。
海勒姆·罗兹·雷维尔斯 (Hiram Rhodes Revels) 于 1870 年成为美国第一位黑人参议员。密西西比州最后一位黑人参议员布兰奇·K·布鲁斯 (Blanche K. Bruce) 一直任职到 1881 年。
快速赶上：选举日后，竞选仍然势均力敌，科罗姆的胜利扩大了民主党在参议院以 55 比 44 领先共和党的优势。
总体情况：科洛姆的胜利是在民主党支出和组织后期激增之后，特朗普在 2024 年在该州领先 23 个百分点。
海德·史密斯在竞选的最后几个月面临着警告信号，尽管科罗姆在总体现金优势方面拥有优势，但她筹集的资金却是这位共和党参议员的两倍。
她在电视广告上的支出也超过了左倾政治行动委员会和超级政治行动委员会的大量广告，以推动对科洛姆的支持，并攻击这位参议员投票不公开与被定罪的人口贩运者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦有关的文件。
海德·史密斯的竞选活动也因她在密西西比州杰克逊接受 WLOX-TV 采访时笨手笨脚地回答了有关牛肉价格的问题而受到批评，她说密西西比人有“太多其他蛋白质可供选择”。
科罗姆的竞选团队利用了她的错误，制作了一个病毒式的竞选广告，敦促选民“选择另一位参议员”。
共和党后来做出了努力来帮助海德-史密斯，包括特朗普总统在奥尔康县的一次集会上为她发表讲话，他在 2024 年以 68% 的优势获胜。
但这还不够。海德-史密斯的任期将在八年后结束。
2018 年，她被时任密西西比州州长菲尔·布莱恩特 (Phil Bryant) 任命为参议员，并于 2020 年竞选完整任期，当时她以 10 个百分点的优势击败了民主党挑战者迈克·埃斯皮 (Mike Espy)。
放大：科洛姆是一位来自哥伦布的 43 岁地方检察官，他致力于降低生活成本、提高工资和保护乡村医院。
他的竞选活动还吸引了民主党的重量级人物为他竞选，其中包括前总统比尔·克林顿、前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯和佐治亚州参议员拉斐尔·沃诺克。
底线：科罗姆的胜利将密西西比州添加到了民主党在中期选举中取得突破的共和党大本营名单中，其中包括德克萨斯州和南卡罗来纳州。
这也强化了黑人选民在民主党东山再起中的作用，此前该党在一个关键投票集团中重新获得了支持，该集团显示出 2024 年转向特朗普的迹象。

title_en: John Thune seeks another term as Senate Republican leader as the party reckons with election losses
title_zh: 约翰·图恩寻求连任参议院共和党领袖，因为该党正面临选举失利
summary: Senate Republicans will be meeting for what they call a “robust conversation” on their future and to decide whether to keep South Dakota Sen. John Thune as their leader
summary_zh: 参议院共和党人将举行会议，就他们的未来进行所谓的“激烈对话”，并决定是否留住南达科他州参议员约翰·周四
body_en: Senate Republicans will be meeting for what they call a “robust conversation” on their future and to decide whether to keep South Dakota Sen. John Thune as their leader
By MARY CLARE JALONICK Associated Press and STEVEN SLOAN Associated Press

WASHINGTON -- Senate Republicans will meet Tuesday for a “robust conversation” on their future and to decide whether to keep South Dakota Sen. John Thune as their leader, just a week after steep losses in the midterm elections that cost them their majority.

Thune is expected to be reelected, given that he remains popular with fellow Senate Republicans and is running unopposed. But some Republicans who returned to Washington on Monday for the first time since the election wipeout that cost them at least seven seats say it's too soon to endorse the status quo.

“We need to have some real soul-searching,” said Wisconsin Sen. Ron Johnson, who has circulated a letter to the conference asking for a delay in the closed-door, secret-ballot leadership elections. “We can't just continue on business as usual — that kind of defeat demands change.”
Still, Johnson conceded that there's no one else on the ballot.
“That's part of our problem, who would want the job?” he said, turning to a reporter and joking, “Do you want it?”

The angst comes as the party is just beginning to reckon with what the election results mean for GOP lawmakers and how soon they can try to rebuild their ranks. Two additional races remain uncalled in Alaska and Mississippi that could further deplete their numbers.

Thune made clear Monday that the leadership is moving ahead with Senate elections, which will include contests for other party leaders as well. But senators could still seek a vote to delay as they gather Tuesday morning.
Thune said they will have a “very fulsome, robust conversation about where we go from here and then we’ll see what the consensus of the conference is.”
“Ultimately that’s a decision made by Republican senators,” Thune said.
Thune, who replaced Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky as leader in early 2025, has spent much of the last two years navigating President Donald Trump, who has often been at odds with the Senate.

While backing up Trump on most policy, Thune has refused to change Senate rules and scrap the filibuster to pass voting legislation that would require proof of citizenship for all voters — a position that frustrated Trump and enraged some in the president's political base.
But Trump hosted Thune and his family at the White House in October. He said Monday that the GOP leader is “a very fine man.” The election is “up to the Senate,” Trump said.

Thune has made it a point to hear out different viewpoints before he makes major decisions and has maintained close relationships with the rank and file — a different approach from his predecessor, McConnell.

Thune “has widespread support” among Republican senators, said Oklahoma Sen. Jim Lankford, who said he supports having the elections on Tuesday when many of the new GOP senators are already in town for freshman orientation.

玛丽·克莱尔·贾洛尼克 (MARY CLARE JALONICK) 美联社和史蒂文·斯隆 (STEVEN SLOAN) 美联社报道
华盛顿——参议院共和党人将于周二举行会议，就他们的未来进行“激烈对话”，并决定是否继续让南达科他州参议员约翰·图恩(John Thune)继续担任他们的领导人，而就在一周前，他们在中期选举中惨败，失去了多数席位。
鉴于图恩仍然受到参议院共和党同僚的欢迎并且没有遭到反对，他预计将再次当选。但一些自选举惨败导致至少七个席位于周一返回华盛顿以来首次返回华盛顿的共和党人表示，现在认可现状还为时过早。
“我们需要进行一些真正的反省，”威斯康星州参议员罗恩·约翰逊说，他向会议分发了一封信，要求推迟闭门、无记名投票的领导人选举。 “我们不能像往常一样继续经营——这种失败需要改变。”
尽管如此，约翰逊承认选票上没有其他人。
“这是我们问题的一部分，谁会想要这份工作？”他转向记者开玩笑说：“你想要吗？”
焦虑出现之际，该党刚刚开始考虑选举结果对共和党议员意味着什么，以及他们多久才能尝试重建队伍。阿拉斯加和密西西比州还有另外两场比赛尚未召集，这可能会进一步耗尽他们的人数。
图恩周一明确表示，领导层正在推进参议院选举，其中也将包括其他党派领导人的竞选。但参议员们仍可能在周二上午聚集时寻求推迟投票。
图恩表示，他们将进行“一次非常充实、有力的对话，讨论我们下一步的发展方向，然后我们将看看会议达成的共识是什么。”
“最终这是共和党参议员做出的决定，”图恩说。
图恩于 2025 年初取代肯塔基州参议员米奇·麦康奈尔 (Mitch McConnell) 成为领导人，过去两年的大部分时间都在与经常与参议院发生争执的唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 总统打交道。
虽然在大多数政策上支持特朗普，但图恩拒绝改变参议院的规则，并拒绝废除要求所有选民提供公民身份证明的投票立法的阻挠——这一立场让特朗普感到沮丧，并激怒了总统政治基础中的一些人。
但特朗普十月份在白宫接待了图恩和他的家人。他周一表示，共和党领导人是“一个非常好的人”。特朗普表示，选举“取决于参议院”。
图恩在做出重大决定之前非常重视听取不同的观点，并与普通员工保持着密切的关系——这与他的前任麦康奈尔不同。
俄克拉荷马州参议员吉姆·兰克福德表示，图恩在共和党参议员中“得到了广泛支持”。他表示，他支持在周二举行选举，因为许多新任共和党参议员已经在城里参加新生培训。
